column1: # Pulled 2026-08-20 via the Looker MCP. There is no Looker credential in this
# repo, so a scheduled tool CANNOT refresh this -- it is exported by hand, the
# same shape as tools/log_campaign_performance.py parsing Max's Slack replies.
# Refresh procedure and the query filters are in docs/campaign-benchmarks.md.
# THIS IS THE WHOLE POPULATION, not a top-N slice. total_signatures is a
# MEASURE, so it cannot go in filter_expression (Looker 400s: "cannot
# reference aggregate field") -- it filters as a HAVING via the filters map,
# e.g. "9000 to 20036". Pulled in four bands to stay inside the row cap:
# The bands are contiguous and the population is exhausted; a wider limit
# returns nothing further. The mid-range is genuinely near-empty -- only 4
# EN_GB campaigns since 2024 landed between 3,000 and 9,000 signatures.
# The 7 rows under 3,000 are NOT weak campaigns, they are a different
# population: response rates of 0.02%-0.78% against 2.1%-8.4% for every row
# above. They include one explicit "TEST-" program and one list-segment split
# (INB_12th_Meeting-Yahoo, 323 signatures, same petition id 14242 as its
# parent's 22,697). They are KEPT here -- the store is the archive -- and
# excluded at display by MIN_LOOKER_SIGNATURES in tools/make_briefs.py.
# Excluded by the >= 100 filter and therefore absent: warm-up and test
# programs under a DIFFERENT naming format (underscore dates, "TEST_WARM_UP",
# "Warmup", "L1"), all of which carry zero signatures.
# money is EUR. otd = one-time donations, md = monthly donations.
